combinedSelectedCompute.definition: Sum of measured published-body inference/preprocessing, scheduled face/feet inference/preprocessing, and real VRM update compute per sampled video frame. Stages are timed separately; decoding, raster rendering, and candidate/reference-model comparison are excluded. Not wall-clock end-to-end latency.

stability.source: real ONNX inference observations; aggregate only

motionEvidence.criterion: accepted image limb direction changes >=12 degrees; observed bone has >=3 rendered frames

challenge.protocol: repeat one real inferred observation for 14 frames; inject one out-of-image high-confidence spike; restore for 6 frames; remove shoulders/hips for 18 frames while retaining inferred lower segments; restore for 12 frames; remove every observation for 40 frames; restore for 5 frames; 30 Hz. These are observation-fault challenges, not model-accuracy measurements.

motionEvidence.criterion: accepted image limb direction changes >=12 degrees; observed bone has >=3 rendered frames

limitations: These metrics evaluate stability and preservation of accepted observable motion, not 3D pose accuracy.
Monocular torso yaw/pitch and unanchored absolute root are intentionally unobserved.
The fault challenge replays inferred landmarks and injects missing/out-of-image observations; it does not claim new model accuracy.

legacyComparison.protocol: Identical actual decoded-video inference observations and identical avatar rest rig. Pinned legacy geometry and retarget run unchanged at each inference arrival; legacy output holds between 30 Hz display samples, matching the previous app. Current guards and retarget run at 30 Hz. Both exclude initial activation and unprocessed gaps over 100 ms from adjacent-frame changes. No extra ONNX inference is performed.
legacyComparison.newNeutral: rig-relative relaxed upper arms, 10 degrees outward

upper60Percent.source: derived image crop from the pinned official public video
upper60Percent.protocol: Keep the upper or lower 60% of actual decoded RGB pixels, then rerun the published selected body ONNX. At most 90 frames in three contiguous 30-frame intervals (beginning/middle/end); short videos retain all frames. Original capture timestamps remain unchanged; unsampled gaps are missing inputs, not evidence that the person disappeared. Extra inference runs in a separate decoding pass after the CPU comparison.

limitations: CPU timings are actual video inference; no user-GPU performance was measured.
Agreement with a reference model is not accuracy against annotations.
The wholebody path uses the full video rectangle as its person crop; no automatic person detector is included.
VRM humanoid and spring systems execute in Node; raster rendering and textures are excluded.
